data.headline: Boost marketing 30% to defend market share
data.why: The simulation shows the marketing plan lifts cash flow by $9.3k versus doing nothing and beats the steady-rival path by $9.4k. With IKEA expanding second-hand sales and the German kitchen-furniture sector in a deep crisis, retailers need a reason to keep ordering your solid-wood sets instead of switching to cheaper or used alternatives.
data.watch_out: Marketing costs $5.3k upfront and the model still shows a $150 weekly holding cost. If the German retail slump deepens or IKEA's used-furniture push accelerates, the extra spend may not convert to enough reorders, draining cash with no payback until week 15.
data.recheck_when: Reassess at week 8 or if German furniture retail sentiment worsens sharply.
